t27zon:216: The core insight of RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) is: different retrieval strategies capture different relevance signals. FTS5 keyword search captures lexical matching, vector similarity captures semantic relevance, and knowledge-graph neighbors capture relational inference. In many cases, a document may be associated with a query for multiple different reasons. Through RRF fusion, the strengths of multiple retrieval strategies can be combined, yielding better recall than any single strategy. The choice of the constant k=60 is an experimentally validated near-optimal value—too low lets one strategy dominate, too high dilutes the differences between strategies.

zwzheo:225: The strategic significance of ai-memory's support for a zero-LLM mode is often underestimated. In current industry practice, many memory systems treat LLM as a default dependency—summarization, entity extraction, and relational inference all require LLM calls. But this brings two problems: (1) the cost and latency of LLM calls make basic retrieval functions expensive; (2) when the LLM is unavailable, the entire memory system fails. The strategic significance of zero-LLM mode is: basic memory functions should be as reliable as a database index—providing basic storage and retrieval without relying on external AI services. LLM is an enhancement layer, not infrastructure.
